meta.title: AI Plan Score
meta.description: A separate AI scoring of the Business Plan: an AI decision model reads every field, takes each decision in turns and shows how it scored the plan.

title: AI Plan Score
lead: A separate AI scoring of your Business Plan, apart from the app's own calculations.

intro.title: A separate AI scoring of your written plan
intro.body: The AI Plan Score is an AI opinion on how specific, quantified and evidenced the texts of your Business Plan are.

points.calculation: It is not the app's calculation. The Quick Check stays the only calculation, and Pitch completeness still only counts which fields are filled.
points.verdict: It is not a feasibility study and not a funding or investment verdict. Use it to see where the plan is still thin.
points.models: Jev, an AI decision model, takes every decision. The text model you choose only writes the report from Jev's numbers and never changes them.

flow.lead: Every decision Jev took, turn by turn, from the first field to the last. Select a node to see its details.

how.title: How the flow decides
how.read: Turn 0, without AI: the app checks which plan parts have text. Empty ones score 0 for certain and are never sent. A complete Quick Check result enters as a fixed signal.
how.turns: Turns 1 to 4, one Jev call per Business Plan step: Jev rates each filled plan part on five levels (missing, vague, specific, quantified, evidenced) and returns a probability for each level. The expected level is E = Σ k · p(k), for k from 0 to 4.
how.gates: Checks are yes or no questions across the plan. They never add points. A check that fails with confidence caps its dimension at level 2 or 3; an unclear answer is only a flag. Some checks are decided by a rule before any AI.
how.branches: Branches are choices, such as the main heat source. The option Jev picks decides which follow-up check the next turn asks.
how.aggregate: Aggregate, without AI: a dimension is the mean of its plan parts, cut by the lowest cap of its failed checks. The AI Plan Score is the weighted sum of the seven dimensions, from 0 to 100, with a band of one standard deviation. Early below 40, Promising from 40, Solid from 70; a failed must-have check keeps it below Solid.
how.report: Report: the text model you chose writes a short report from these numbers. It cannot change them.

early.name: Early
early.description: The plan names the idea but leaves most of what makes a plan solid open.

promising.name: Promising
promising.description: The plan is specific in many places; some parts still lack numbers, evidence or clear roles.

solid.name: Solid
solid.description: The plan is specific, quantified and backed by evidence in most places, and no must-have check failed.

missing.name: Missing
missing.description: Empty, a placeholder or not about this item or site.

vague.name: Vague
vague.description: A general claim that could fit any project: no named actor, place or number.

specific.name: Specific
specific.description: Names the actors, buildings, sources or mechanisms of this site, without numbers or a basis for them.

quantified.name: Quantified
quantified.description: Gives the key quantities with units and a stated basis or assumption.

evidenced.name: Evidenced
evidenced.description: The numbers are backed by named data or commitments, or tested, and the text says what happens if one is wrong.

value.name: Customer value and demand
value.description: Who connects, what they need and why the network beats their alternative.

technology.name: Technical and site fit
technology.description: The site, its heat sources and resources, and whether the network fits the place.

economics.name: Costs, revenues and financing
economics.description: Costs, tariffs, financing and subsidies, and whether revenues cover the costs over the lifetime.

governance.name: Ownership, operation and governance
governance.description: Who owns, operates and pays for what, and how costs, risks and benefits are split.

participation.name: Participation and commitment
participation.description: Owners, stakeholders, the anchor customer and the connection rate the plan relies on.

evidence.name: Risks, assumptions and evidence
evidence.description: Critical assumptions and risks, the deal-breaker and how each is validated.

path.name: Implementation path and scalability
path.description: The first phase, the next steps, the decision gate and how the model grows.

judgements.allocation: Allocation of investment, risk and benefit
judgements.decisions: Key decisions and the decision gate

anchor.name: Anchor customer
anchor.question: Does the plan name at least one specific anchor customer, a large or early connection, and its role?

extra-value.name: Extra value
extra-value.question: Does the plan use cooling or another extra value, such as stable prices or relief for the power grid, as a reason to connect, where it applies?

heat-density.name: Network length as a cost driver
heat-density.question: Does the plan address network length or heat line density as a cost driver, for example trench length, clustering close buildings or micro-networks?

vienna-zone.name: Zone in the Vienna Heating Plan 2040
vienna-zone.question: Does the plan state the site's zone in the Vienna Heating Plan 2040 and explain why a 5GDHC network fits it?

boundary.name: System boundary
boundary.question: Who owns the heat source, the network and the heat pumps in the buildings, according to the plan?

operator.name: Operator and duties
operator.question: Does the plan name an operator and its operational duties, such as maintenance, billing, faults and security of supply?

cost-key.name: Cost key
cost-key.question: Does the plan state a rule for splitting the costs of the source, the pipes and the connections among the users?

price-vs-alternative.name: Price against the alternative
price-vs-alternative.question: Is the customer's price compared with the customer's realistic alternative, such as gas or an individual heat pump, including price stability?

connection-threshold.name: Minimum connection rate
connection-threshold.question: Does the plan state a connection rate and what happens to the costs or the viability if fewer buildings connect?

lifetime-cover.name: Revenues cover the lifetime costs
lifetime-cover.question: Does the plan compare the yearly revenues with the yearly cost of the investment plus the running costs, heat-pump electricity included, over 20 to 30 years?

subsidy-dependence.name: Subsidy fallback
subsidy-dependence.question: How does the plan depend on subsidies?

deal-breaker.name: Deal-breaker with a validation
deal-breaker.question: Is one risk marked as the potential deal-breaker, could it really stop the project, and does it have a concrete validation step (what, who, when)?

start-small.name: Start small
start-small.question: Is a first phase defined, such as an anchor cluster or a micro-network, with later steps to grow?

decision-gate.name: Decision gate
decision-gate.question: Do the next steps contain a go or no-go decision with explicit, checkable criteria?

anchor-public.name: Public decision path
anchor-public.question: Does the plan address the public owner's decision path: a council or board decision, the budget, or public procurement?

anchor-commercial.name: Anchor contract term
anchor-commercial.question: Does the plan address how long the commercial anchor customer commits (contract term) compared with the payback period of the network?

anchor-residential.name: How owners and tenants decide
anchor-residential.question: Does the plan address how the individual owners or tenants decide, for example owners' votes, tenancy rules or consent of the tenants?

anchor-industry.name: Secure waste heat or cooling demand
anchor-industry.question: Does the plan address how secure the waste heat or the cooling demand is over time: a contract, and a backup if the company leaves?

water-permit.name: Permit route for water or ground
water-permit.question: Does the plan name the permit route for using the groundwater, the ground or the surface water, or an early check with the water authority?

source-wastewater.name: Sewer operator and wastewater data
source-wastewater.question: Does the plan address an agreement with the sewer operator and the measured flow and temperature of the wastewater?

source-waste-heat.name: Waste-heat supply agreement
source-waste-heat.question: Does the plan address a supply agreement with the owner of the waste heat and what happens if that supply stops?

source-air.name: Air source in cold weather
source-air.question: Does the plan address the lower efficiency of air as a source in cold weather and the noise of the outdoor units?

owner-utility.name: Utility commitment
owner-utility.question: Does the plan state the utility's commitment: a decision, a letter of intent or its defined role in the project?

owner-municipal.name: Municipal decision path
owner-municipal.question: Does the plan address the municipal decision path: a council decision, the budget or a municipal company?

owner-community.name: Community rules
owner-community.question: Does the plan address the rules of the community: members' votes, joining and leaving, liability and how members finance their share?

owner-contracting.name: Contract term and prices
owner-contracting.question: Does the plan address the contract term, how prices may change over time and what happens when the contract ends?

owner-developer.name: Operation after handover
owner-developer.question: Does the plan address who operates and maintains the network after the buildings are handed over or sold?

boundary.partial: Owner of one or two stated

anchor-type.name: Anchor type
anchor-type.question: Which kind of anchor customer does the plan mainly rely on?

source-type.name: Main heat source
source-type.question: Which heat source does the plan mainly rely on?

ownership.name: Ownership model
ownership.question: Which ownership and operating model does the plan describe for the network?

checks.title: Checks and decisions
checks.lead: Checks are yes-or-no or choice questions across the plan. They never add points: a check that fails with confidence caps its dimension, an unclear one is only a flag. The branches decide which follow-up check the next turn asks.
checks.meterLabel: Probability that it passes: {value}. Passes from {pass}, fails up to {fail}.
checks.capPossible: Would cap {dimension} at level {level} if it failed
checks.capConditional: Would cap {dimension} at level {level} if it failed while the Quick Check heat density is low
checks.flag: A flag only: it never lowers the score
checks.refusedBranch: Jev gave no answer, so no follow-up check was asked.

report.title: Short report
report.lead: Written by the text model from Jev's final numbers. It never changes a number.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.lead: On request, the text model suggests general, feasible improvements for weak plan parts (below level {level}) and for checks that failed or stayed unclear. Nothing is sent until you ask.
suggestions.ask: Suggest improvements for the weak parts
suggestions.askAgain: Suggest again for the weak parts
suggestions.nothing: No weak plan parts and no failed or unclear checks: nothing to suggest.

how.title: How we score
how.lead: The AI Plan Score turns Jev's decisions into numbers without further AI. Every number here comes from the method itself.

levels.title: {count} evidence levels
levels.lead: Every plan part is judged on the same scale. The levels describe quality, never length.

turns.title: Turns
turns.lead: Turn 0 reads the plan without AI: empty parts score 0 and are never sent, and the Quick Check enters as a fixed signal. Then Jev takes one turn per Business Plan step, from the first field to the last, and sees the options it chose in the choice questions of earlier turns.

checks.title: Checks and caps
checks.body: A check passes when Jev puts its probability at {pass} or above and fails at {fail} or below; in between it stays unclear and is only a flag. A failed check caps its dimension at level {caps}. A failed must-have check caps at level {mustHave} and keeps the label below {solid}. A flag never caps.

branches.title: Branches and follow-up checks
branches.body: The choice questions {names} pick the follow-up check the next turn asks, so each plan gets the questions that fit it.
branches.name: “{name}”

formulas.title: Formulas

expected.name: Expected level of a plan part

dimensionLevel.name: Level of a dimension
dimensionLevel.formula: L = min(mean E of its parts, lowest cap of its failed checks)

choicePass.name: Pass probability of a choice check
choicePass.formula: P = Σ v(o) · p(o) / Σ p(o); v = {pass} for a passing option, {partial} for a partial one, {fail} for a failing one; options that do not apply are left out

formulas.note: An empty part counts as 0 with no spread; a part without an answer does not count. The spread of a dimension takes its parts as independent, which probably understates it.

weights.title: Weights
weights.lead: Reasoned defaults that sum to {total}; no source prescribes numbers.

labels.title: Labels
labels.solid: {solid} and above, unless a must-have check failed
labels.rounding: Shown rounded to {step} points, with the band in whole points and at least {minBand}, to avoid false precision. The label uses the unrounded score.

caveats.title: Read it with care
caveats.calibration: Jev's probabilities are not calibrated: 80 % does not mean it is right four times in five.
caveats.opinion: The score is an AI opinion on the written plan, not a prediction of feasibility or funding.
caveats.length: Length is not quality: a longer text scores higher only when it is more specific, quantified or evidenced.

remove.title: Delete the AI Plan Score?
remove.body: The saved score, its report and its suggestions are removed from this project. Your Business Plan stays as it is, and you can score again at any time.
